attributes.probed_form: SIX KEEPS, each measured separately. (1) POLARITY, three sites, verbatim: `cv = -1.0f; if (pct < 1.0) { cv = ...; }` -> `if (pct >= 1.0) { cv = -1.0f; } else { cv = ...; }`; `cv = 0.0f; if (0.0 < (f32)(pct - 1.0)) { cv = ...; }` -> `if ((f32)(pct - 1.0) <= 0.0) { cv = 0.0f; } else { cv = ...; }`; and the same rewrite on `0.0 < HealthMeterValue[meter] / HealthMeterMaxValue[meter]`. (2) HOIST + integer polarity: added `flags2 = HealthMeter668[meter];` beside `flags = HealthMeter65C[meter];` (the target loads BOTH before the NPieces test: `@0xb8 lwz r6,84(r4)` / `@0xbc lwz r0,48(r4)` / `@0xc0 lwz r7,96(r4)`, and reads them again at `@0x124 subfic r0,r6,256` and `@0x2b0 add r0,r6,r7`), plus `if (v < nv)` -> `if (nv > v)` and `if (pausecnt < 1) { 0xffffffff } else { 0xff8080ff }` -> `if (pausecnt > 0) { 0xff8080ff } else { 0xffffffff }`. (3) CAST WIDTH: `(f32)(0.00390625 * (f32)a2)` -> `(f32)(0.00390625 * a2)` and `(f32)(0.00390625 * (f32)(int)cv)` -> `a1 = (int)cv;` + `(f32)(0.00390625 * a1)`; the FIRST of the three 0.00390625 sites keeps its `(f32)a1` cast because the target emits fsubs there (`@0x218 fsubs f0,f0,f2`) and fsub at the other two (`@0x264`, `@0x31c`). (4) SHORT-CIRCUIT: `if (fg[0]==0) return; if (fg[1]==0) return;` -> `if (fg[0]==0 || fg[1]==0) return;`. (5) `void* blit = HealthMeterBG[meter][i]; if (blit != 0)` -> `if (HealthMeterBG[meter][i] != 0)` with the expression repeated in both arms. (6) `pct = (f32)(pct - 1.0);` as its own statement before the guard, and `pct = HealthMeterValue[meter] / HealthMeterMaxValue[meter];` as its own statement in the else arm. NEGATIVE PROBES, both reverted: (a) wrapping the NPieces==2 body in an explicit `else { }` after `if (fg[1]==0) { return; }` — MWCC folds the else and the `beq` is unchanged (this is why the `||` form is the right one: the target's `@0xdc beq ->388` on the FIRST test and `@0xec bne ->f4 / @0xf0 b ->388` on the second is a branch-to-branch fold of one disjunction, not two independent early returns); (b) swapping the source operands of the else-arm multiply to `(f32)(256 - (flags + flags2)) * ratio` — byte-identical output, the commutative canonicalisation law.
